clue.text: Peel's first deed, producing treaty

indicators.note: Peel's first means the opening letter of the word Peel

parts.note: a deed is something done, an act

explanation.surface: Sir Robert Peel's first official act as a statesman leads to an international agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact is a formal agreement between parties, a synonym for a treaty.

clue.text: Buy leverage

definitions.meaning: to acquire something by paying for it
a firm hold or grip giving mechanical advantage

explanation.definitionFit: Purchase means both an acquisition by payment and a grip or foothold giving leverage.

clue.text: Conspirator involved in Guernica's capture?

indicators.note: the answer is wrapped up inside the words Guernica's capture

explanation.surface: Asks whether some plotter was behind the seizure of the Spanish town Guernica.
explanation.definitionFit: Casca was one of the conspirators who stabbed Julius Caesar, first to strike in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Steal a Kandinsky painting, for example?

definitions.meaning: Kandinsky was a pioneer of non-representational art, so one of his canvases is an example of that kind of work

explanation.surface: An art thief's plan to make off with a Kandinsky canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstract as a verb means take away or purloin; as a noun it is a non-figurative artwork, like Kandinsky's.

clue.text: Chicken thieves may do it, and also if caught in the act!

definitions.text: Chicken thieves may do it, and also if caught in the act!

parts.words: Chicken thieves may do it, and also if caught in the act
parts.note: thieves after hens force entry into a pen for poultry, and when spotted they suddenly start sprinting away

explanation.surface: Poultry thieves at work, and what they do when someone spots them.
explanation.walkthrough: A run is also a chicken enclosure, so the phrase works twice: breaking into a pen, and starting to sprint away.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to start running, and literally to force entry into a hen enclosure.

clue.text: Mousy chap a girl's thrown over

parts.note: Tim is a man's name, a chap

indicators.note: thrown over means turned the other way, so the girl's name is read backwards

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name

explanation.surface: A shy man who has been jilted by his girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown over' reads as being jilted by a girlfriend, but it is the reversal signal; the possessive 's is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Mousy describes a shy, quiet, nervous person, which is what timid means.

clue.text: Fruit provided by a very old accountant at party

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
a do is an informal party

explanation.surface: Fruit brought along by an elderly accountant to a party.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocado is the pear-shaped fruit of a tropical tree.

clue.text: Arduous march leaders of the Royal Engineers finally undertook

indicators.note: the leaders of the three words are their opening letters
finally picks the closing letter of undertook

explanation.surface: Army engineers' officers completed a gruelling hike.
explanation.definitionFit: A trek is a long, hard journey on foot, a gruelling march.

clue.text: Delay in violent robbery?

definitions.meaning: a hitch or wait, as in a traffic jam
an armed robbery, as of a bank or a stagecoach

explanation.definitionFit: A hold-up is both a delay to progress and a robbery carried out at gunpoint.

clue.text: Rhode Island's one and only savoury dish?

parts.note: RI is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Rhode Island, with S from the possessive
sole means single, the one and only

explanation.surface: A boast that some Rhode Island dish is unique to the state.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is not a link here: it supplies the S after RI.
explanation.definitionFit: A rissole is a fried cake of minced meat or fish, a savoury dish.

clue.text: Rodent has change of heart, seeing big creature with horns

indicators.note: the central letter of the word for the rodent is swapped for a different one

parts.note: a mouse is a small rodent

explanation.surface: A rodent's sudden change of mind on seeing a large horned beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has change of heart' swaps the middle letter U of MOUSE for O.
explanation.definitionFit: The moose is the largest deer, a big animal with broad antlers.

clue.text: Picked up sound made by group of animals, say

indicators.note: the answer is the sound of a word, so we hear rather than read it
say signals the answer is spoken like the word for the group of animals

parts.note: a herd is a group of cattle or other animals

explanation.surface: Someone caught the noise of a herd of animals.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up a noise is to hear it, so picked up is the past tense equivalent.

clue.text: Abduct child, then take forty winks

parts.note: a kid is informal for a child
forty winks is a short sleep, so take forty winks means nap

explanation.surface: A kidnapper's plan: snatch a child, then have a snooze.
explanation.definitionFit: To kidnap someone is to abduct them, carrying them off by force.

clue.text: Display greater ferocity to confuse

definitions.meaning: to show more savagery, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: Bewilder means to perplex; split in two it reads 'be wilder', to act more fiercely.

clue.text: Way Essex town's character is an aid to progress

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
Epping is a town in Essex, with S from the possessive
tone is the character or quality of something

explanation.surface: The ethos of a particular Essex town is said to help people get on.
explanation.walkthrough: EPPING is a market town in Essex, just north-east of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepping stone, literally a stone to cross a stream, figuratively means a stage helping one advance.

clue.text: Blissfully happy Welsh girl supporting Cambs city

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporter goes underneath, so the girl's name comes after the city

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, abbreviated Cambs
Sian is a Welsh girl's name

explanation.surface: A Welsh woman delighted to be backing a city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Elysian, from Elysium the paradise of Greek myth, means heavenly or blissful.

clue.text: Damages booty

explanation.definitionFit: Spoils is a verb meaning ruins and a plural noun meaning loot seized by victors.

clue.text: Energetic person's awful Monday!

indicators.note: something awful is in a dreadful state, so the letters of Monday are jumbled

explanation.surface: Even a lively go-getter can have a terrible start to the week.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo, a generator of power, is a figurative term for a tirelessly energetic person.

clue.text: Expert in a small section of store

parts.note: Dept is the short form of department, a section of a store

explanation.surface: A specialist working in one corner of a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Adept as a noun is a skilled person, a synonym for an expert.

clue.text: Daggers supplied by old boy and priest

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
Eli is the priest in the Bible who brought up Samuel

explanation.surface: Weapons handed over by a former pupil and a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeli are dagger-shaped printing marks, the plural of obelus, used for footnotes.

clue.text: Exceptionally wide, for example

definitions.meaning: ... means especially or unusually, as in ... large
in cricket a wide is a ball out of the batsman's reach, one kind of run not scored off the bat

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a wide is a run given away when the bowler sends the ball out of reach; such runs are called extras.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra serves as an adverb meaning especially, and as a cricket term covering wides, byes and no-balls.

clue.text: Possesses penny to get hinged plate

parts.note: has means owns or possesses

explanation.surface: Someone with a coin wants a hinged metal fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A hasp is a hinged metal strap that fits over a staple and is secured by a padlock.

clue.text: In maturity the Italian is nimble

indicators.note: In tells us the Italian article goes inside the word for maturity

parts.note: age can mean maturity, as in coming of age
il is the Italian for the

explanation.surface: An Italian who stays nimble even in old age.
explanation.definitionFit: Agile and nimble are synonyms, both meaning quick and light in movement.

clue.text: Recently clothed in bright colour — as mother and daughter are

indicators.note: one word is dressed in the other, so the word for recently sits inside the colour

parts.note: red is a bright colour
late can mean recently, as in of late

explanation.surface: Mother and daughter have just been dressed in matching bright outfits.
explanation.definitionFit: Mother and daughter are kin, connected by family, so they are relations.

clue.text: Regretful writer, one given shelter

parts.note: a pen is something to write with
I is the Roman numeral for one
a tent is a canvas shelter

explanation.surface: A remorseful author who has been given somewhere to stay.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone penitent is sorry for wrongdoing, so regretful is a close synonym.

clue.text: Musical atmosphere met by Handel at first

indicators.note: the air is met by, so placed after, the letter from Handel
at first takes only the opening letter of the composer's name

parts.note: air is the atmosphere around us

explanation.surface: A musical mood meets the work of the composer Handel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical' looks like an adjective describing atmosphere, but it is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair is the 1960s rock musical famous for its hippie theme, so it is an example of a musical.
